sections.title: Basic Concept of Coding-Decoding
sections.content: Coding-Decoding is a part of Logical Reasoning where a word, letter, or sentence is changed into another form based on a specific rule. In coding, the original word is transformed. In decoding, we find the original word from the coded form. The main skill required is identifying the hidden pattern.

sections.title: Alphabet Position Method
sections.content: In the English alphabet, A=1, B=2, C=3 up to Z=26. Many questions are based on adding or subtracting numbers from these positions. Example: CAT → C=3, A=1, T=20. If each letter is increased by 1, the new word becomes DBU.

sections.title: Simple Letter Shifting
sections.content: Sometimes each letter in a word is moved forward or backward by a fixed number. Example: DOG becomes FQI if each letter is shifted by +2.

sections.title: Reverse Word Pattern
sections.content: In some questions, the word is simply written in reverse order. Example: RAM becomes MAR.

sections.title: Letter Sum Method
sections.content: Add the position values of all letters in a word to get a number code. Example: BAT → B=2, A=1, T=20. Total = 23.

sections.title: Sentence Coding Basics
sections.content: In sentence coding, each word is replaced by a code word or symbol. Identify common words in different sentences to find their codes.

sections.title: Important Tips
sections.content: 1. First check alphabet positions. 2. Look for +1 or -1 patterns. 3. Check if the word is reversed. 4. Compare similar words carefully.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Forgetting alphabet positions. 2. Ignoring simple patterns. 3. Making calculation errors. 4. Selecting an answer without checking all options.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Coding-Decoding at Level 1 mainly includes alphabet positions, simple shifting, reversing words, and basic sentence coding. Practice helps improve speed and accuracy.

tricks.title: Alphabet Position Memory Trick
tricks.explanation: Remember A=1 to Z=26 clearly. M is 13 and Z is 26.
tricks.example: If asked about the position of K, it is 11.

tricks.title: Opposite Letter Rule
tricks.explanation: Opposite letters in the alphabet add up to 27.

tricks.title: Check +1 or -1 First
tricks.explanation: Most basic questions use +1 or -1 shifting.

tricks.title: Reverse Checking Trick
tricks.explanation: Always check if the word is simply reversed.

tricks.title: Letter Sum Shortcut
tricks.explanation: Quickly add letter positions to see if the answer is a number.

tricks.title: Common Word Identification
tricks.explanation: In sentence coding, identify repeated words first.
tricks.example: If RAM appears twice with same code, that code belongs to RAM.

tricks.title: Option Elimination Trick
tricks.explanation: Remove options that clearly do not follow the pattern.
